memory_candidates.content: Before extracting a new shared shell-lib for a measured boilerplate pattern, grep the corpus's existing libs for the target function names first -- scripts/lib/common.sh already carried common_test_pass/_fail/_info (byte-identical to a planned new harness's pass/fail/info trio) unused by any of 122 core test suites. Building a second library would have been a net-addition duplicate of the exact kind the enclosing task's net-deletion acceptance criterion exists to catch.

A sourced bash library function that needs to install an EXIT trap referencing a value it just computed (e.g. `WORKDIR=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$WORKDIR"' EXIT`) must never be called via command substitution (`WORKDIR="$(fn)"`) -- command substitution forks its own subshell, whose EXIT fires the trap (deleting the resource) the instant the function returns, before the outer assignment can read anything. The function must be called as a bare statement and read back via the global variable it sets.
